candidates.topic: FDA recalls millions of bottles of eye drops nationwide
candidates.recommended_angle: Service-journalism safety explainer: what's affected, why, and what consumers should do with bottles they already own — framed against the pattern of a very active 2026 recall year.
candidates.why_now: Breaking same-day FDA notice covering millions of units — not previously covered; distinct from this week's Gatorade/Salata/BP-medication recalls.
candidates.primary_headline: FDA Recalls Millions of Eye Drop Bottles Nationwide — What to Check Before You Use Yours
candidates.next_steps: Confirm FDA.gov primary enforcement notice and lot codes before publish; publish today.
integrity_flags: Confirm exact FDA enforcement report number and lot codes directly via FDA.gov before publishing — only one secondary outlet captured in today's signal set.
candidates.trend_score_reason: Single-day breaking news with millions of units affected; distinct from prior week's recall cluster
candidates.opportunity_score_reason: High consumer search intent for 'is my product recalled' + natural service-journalism angle; strong AI-citation candidate once FDA notice confirmed
candidates.discover_score_reason: Specific entity, product-focused recall with practical consumer action items (check lot number, stop use)
candidates.notes: Evidence requirement: moderate — recall details, lot numbers, FDA contamination findings. Estimated word count 600–800.

fact_check.checked_against: Prevention article in Google News Radar (FDA recall health) dated 10/08/2026 matching headline and claim of millions of units; confirmed distinct from Gatorade/Salata/BP recall items also in radar

candidates.topic: Early clinical trial: Type 1 diabetes patients able to go off insulin
candidates.recommended_angle: Measured explainer that separates the real finding (early-phase, small cohort) from the headline implication of a cure — what's proven, what's not, and who it could eventually help.
candidates.why_now: New NBC News report on early clinical trial result, not previously covered; T1D audience has high evidence-seeking interest.
candidates.primary_headline: In Early Trial, People With Type 1 Diabetes Went Off Insulin — Here's What That Actually Means
candidates.next_steps: Confirm trial name, phase, institution, and sample size directly before publish; do not rely on headline framing alone.
integrity_flags: Early-phase and small-cohort result — do not frame as a cure. Clarify study phase, sample size, and follow-up duration once primary source is confirmed.
candidates.trend_score_reason: Early-phase clinical trial result with high patient-audience interest; breaking news angle via NBC
candidates.opportunity_score_reason: High AI-citation potential — specific named trial, natural question format ('can type 1 diabetes be cured'), durable topic
candidates.discover_score_reason: Highest discovery potential among candidates — chronic disease, natural curiosity format, seeks nuance on early-phase vs. approved treatment
candidates.notes: Evidence requirement: heavy — chronic disease treatment claim requires peer-reviewed or named-trial sourcing. Estimated word count 700–900.

fact_check.checked_against: NBC News headline in Google News Radar (clinical trial health) dated 10/04/2026 matching topic and headline framing

candidates.topic: Study finds microglia play protective role in Parkinson's disease
candidates.recommended_angle: Explain what the finding actually shows (likely preclinical), why it complicates the standard 'inflammation is bad' Parkinson's narrative, and what it means for future treatment research.
candidates.why_now: New study coverage (10/07), no prior coverage of this specific finding; complements existing Parkinson's research discussions.
candidates.primary_headline: Scientists Find a Surprising Protective Role for Brain Cells in Parkinson's Disease
candidates.next_steps: Verify journal, DOI, and model type (animal vs. human) before publishing; contact neurologist for independent context.
integrity_flags: Confirm whether finding is from an animal/preclinical model or human tissue/data — do not generalize to patient treatment implications without qualification.
candidates.trend_score_reason: Niche but legitimate neuroscience research; limited search velocity but qualified academic audience
candidates.opportunity_score_reason: Moderate AI-citation potential — specific finding, but likely preclinical, which caps durability of practical takeaway
candidates.discover_score_reason: Preclinical research finding; lower general-audience discovery intent; specialized Parkinson's audience
candidates.notes: Evidence requirement: heavy — neuroscience/disease mechanism claim must name journal and clarify model type. Estimated word count 600–750.
